claim: The settled 2026 practitioner pattern is to route 60-80% of agent traffic to a self-hosted Qwen 3 Coder or Kimi K2.6 setup and escalate the hardest 20-40% to Claude Opus 4.7 or Gemini 3.1 Pro.
quote: route 60-80% of agent traffic to a self-hosted Qwen 3 Coder or Kimi K2.6 setup, escalate the remaining 20-40% to Claude Opus 4.7 or Gemini 3.1 Pro.

claim: Local models like Qwen 3 Coder 32B are productive for daily coding but fall short of frontier on hard refactors and deep reasoning, where teams still escalate.
quote: It will not match Claude Opus 4.7 on a hard refactor, but it will handle most of what you do in a day.

claim: Local 7B models score 10-20 percentage points below GPT-5.5 on reasoning and reach only 45-55% HumanEval versus GPT-5.5's 90%, while CPU inference runs 4-10x slower.
quote: Local 7B models score 10-20 percentage points below GPT-5.5 on reasoning... Code generation: local 7B achieves 45-55% HumanEval vs GPT-5.5's 90%.

claim: Local LLMs win on privacy (data never leaves device, no DPAs needed) and cost at scale, breaking even in 6-12 months for heavy users above ~10M tokens/month.
quote: ~$0/token (after hardware) for local vs $0.01-0.05 per 1K tokens for cloud... Local breaks even in 6-12 months for heavy users (>10M tokens/month).

claim: The HN consensus is that the 2026 bottleneck is no longer code generation speed but verification capacity, and that orchestrating bounded workflows beats raw model autonomy.
quote: The core bottleneck in 2026 is no longer code generation speed. It is verification capacity.

claim: Hacker News commenters argue open models are now good enough for the broad industry, with usable capability runnable on cheap used hardware like a $200 16GB GPU.
quote: open models are now good enough. The boasting of models so good they can't be shared was propaganda to frame the conversation.

claim: Indie hackers in 2026 are canceling API subscriptions to run production agents locally; the OllamaClaude project uses Claude Code as orchestrator while delegating coding to local Ollama models, claiming up to 98.75% reduction in Anthropic API token usage.
quote: The OllamaClaude project on GitHub uses Claude Code as an orchestrator but delegates the actual coding work to local Ollama models, claiming up to 98.75% reduction in Anthropic API token usage.

claim: Highest-ROI local wins in 2026 are batch/real-time tasks like content moderation (sub-500ms via local Ollama), ticket summarization, and embeddings, where local beats cloud on cost and control.
quote: real-time content moderation using local Ollama inference... delivers sub-500ms latency and privacy, outperforming cloud APIs in cost and control.

claim: Research shows strong reasoning models still fail at long-horizon planning because chain-of-thought is greedy step-wise scoring, not planning, explaining why local (and even frontier) models struggle on long-horizon agentic tasks.
quote: reasoning is not planning... Improving local reasoning alone is insufficient to yield coherent long-horizon planning, regardless of whether it is obtained via prompting, beam search, or reinforcement learning.

claim: Production local deployments cut costs sharply: one March 2026 batch deployment ran $1,280/month (3 instances + storage) versus a prior $6,700/month cloud API bill.
quote: A March 2026 production deployment showed monthly infrastructure cost of $1,280 (3 instances + storage) vs the previous $6,700 monthly cloud API bill.
